authority: Vane's ruling on the provider-version question (2026-11-21, ~/workspace/duenna-fix/VANE-PINNING-RULING-2026-11-21.md): the pinned catalogue snapshot does NOT satisfy Rev 4 SS8-SS9's provider-version requirement; it stands as a catalogue identity/configuration anchor only.
document: Constitution annex ADDENDUM — correction round (2026-11-21). The original constitution_annex.json is untouched; this addendum sits beside it and governs the provider-version fields it names.
eligibility_status: UNRESOLVED ELIGIBILITY CONDITION for both routes — expressly NOT an exclusion of Groq or NVIDIA, and NOT a satisfaction of the pin. The distinction is preserved for the design decision (Ben / a design revision settled with Vane).
gemini_note: The Gemini route is untouched by this addendum (excluded in the build round on the D1 live-delivery failure; its catalogue version field '001' stands as recorded in the original annex).

catalogue_snapshot_identity_anchor.role: catalogue identity and configuration anchor ONLY — binds the advertised model ID, owner, and full catalogue entry; does NOT establish the actual serving-model version and cannot detect a silent backend change

search_record.disposition: Whether a pinned system_fingerprint (recorded per trial and compared across the round) satisfies the provider-version requirement is RETURNED FOR AN EXPLICIT DESIGN DECISION. The build does not claim that it does, does not waive the requirement, and does not reinterpret it.
search_record.found: Groq chat responses carry system_fingerprint (observed value fp_2166f87c46 on the probe response), documented by Groq as the fingerprint of 'the backend configuration that the model runs with', usable 'to understand when backend changes have been made'. It is a backend-change signal, NOT a version identifier: it does not name or establish the serving model's version.

groq.statement: The complete provider-version pin is NOT satisfied for this route. The Groq catalogue entry exposes no provider-version field, and no provider-supported version identifier was found (see search record).

catalogue_snapshot_identity_anchor.role: catalogue identity and configuration anchor ONLY — as above

search_record.disposition: Recorded as a limitation RETURNED FOR AN EXPLICIT DESIGN DECISION. Not waived, not reinterpreted, not resolved in the build.
search_record.found: No provider-supported version identifier and no independently verifiable serving-version attestation exists on the surfaces reachable through the existing connector.

nvidia.statement: The complete provider-version pin is NOT satisfied for this route. The NVIDIA hosted catalogue entry contains only id/object/created/owned_by, the chat response body contains no fingerprint or version field, the response headers carry no version information, and the NIM management endpoints that report version on self-hosted containers (/v1/version, /v1/metadata, /v1/manifest) return HTTP 404 on the hosted integrate.api.nvidia.com surface.
